subject.title: fix(security): bound plugin manifest reads in audit deep scan

question: Should the deep security audit adopt a 1 MiB plugin-manifest ceiling even though oversized manifests can prevent discovery of declared entrypoints outside the plugin directory?
rationale: The implementation is correct and proven, but the threshold and reduced fallback scan coverage are security-policy tradeoffs that require owner intent.

options.title: Approve the audit boundary
options.body: Accept the 1 MiB ceiling and existing warning-plus-directory-scan fallback as the intended defense-in-depth behavior.

options.title: Revise the boundary first
options.body: Choose or centralize a different manifest limit and preserve any additional scan coverage required for oversized manifests before merging.

recommendation.title: Approve the audit boundary
recommendation.body: Accept the 1 MiB ceiling and existing warning-plus-directory-scan fallback as the intended defense-in-depth behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged and directly hardened the scanner’s observable-failure path that this PR changes.
